statusMapping.403: status 403 kept -> page denied/httpStatus 403 -> 'the server rejected this diagnostics read (HTTP 403)'
statusMapping.200 ok/empty/disabled/stale/dropped: passed through unchanged to parseDiagnosticsSnapshot (the page keeps the view-model mapping)
statusMapping.other non-200: passed through; parseDiagnosticsSnapshot maps to error
statusMapping.transport rejection: propagates (Command turns it into the error state)
statusMapping.non-JSON 2xx body: throws Error('diagnostics read returned a non-JSON body') instead of being shown as empty

originAssumption: Same-origin deployment: the page is served by the runtime host bridge on the same origin as the diagnostics API, so this is a plain same-origin GET (no CORS preflight, no credentials mode). If the page were served elsewhere: an absolute API base URL would be required, the host would need CORS for GET + the authorization header from that origin, and the trust model would change because device-owner trust is socket-peer based, not Origin based - a cross-origin page could never inherit it and would need an explicitly provisioned bearer read credential (never in public assets).
